description:
USER (s488, after reading how the module cache works): "This looks like a rock solid design. Can we realistically extend it to normal scripts too?" -> Fable: YES, and "Please add a todo to look at this for a real implementation."  NOT launched (USER: no new subjob that day).  Supersedes docs/pcl-rollout-plan.md Phase 6 + Phase 7 (their md5(path+mtime) key and mtime-stat'ed deps sidecar predate the content-hash manifest, task #1261; do NOT build them as written -- a script entry IS a module-cache entry).

MEASURED (s488, warm core, cl/pack-impl.pl = 1,211 lines, best of 2-3):
  perl-side transpile (PPI + codegen)           2.26 s
  SBCL loads the .lisp as SOURCE (compiles every form)   3.30 s
  end to end via runpcl today                   5.60 s
  loading the same code from a fasl             0.003 s   (both define the same 22 functions: 18150 -> 18172 fbound symbols)
  bare SBCL start from the cached core          0.003 s
  one-line script end to end today              0.165 s   (0.12 s = the pl2cl process starting)
So a hit takes both shapes to well under 0.1 s (the `pcl` perl driver's own startup + one stat + the manifest's MD5s).

WHY IT DROPS IN: (1) the transpile side already writes the manifest (`pl2cl --deps FILE`; a script miss is that call in PROGRAM mode, so drop announcements stay on -- NOT `--module`); (2) `p-cache-valid-p`, the fasl identity in the filename, `*pcl-fasl-build*` (BEGIN blocks + sub installs move into the fasl as LOAD-time forms; a script's body after `(p-run-compile-phase-blocks)` is plain toplevel forms, so compile-file compiles them WITHOUT running them and load runs them once, in source order -- the discipline that already prevents the #1060 'ran the program at build time' shape), the prune and `--cache-info` are all shared; (3) a script's emission has the same shape as a module's (probed: tiny.pl -> p-defpackage/in-package/defvars/p-run-compile-phase-blocks/body).

WHAT IS NEW (each a guard row):
 a. POLICY: the default compile policy (`PCL_COMPILE_DIRS`/`PCL_NO_COMPILE_DIRS`) never fasl-compiles a file under `.`/`-I`/PERL5LIB (an edited module stays readable text).  The MAIN SCRIPT must be exempt or the cache buys nothing -- a script-specific rule, on by default for `pcl FILE` (it cannot change behaviour: same predicate as modules; loud source fallback when compile-file fails), `--no-cache` / PCL_NO_CACHE off.  Rollout plan said opt-in `--cache`; Fable recommends default-on; USER decides.
 b. KEYING: `-e`/`-E` code and the temp file `pcl` writes for `-M` prefixes must NOT be keyed by path (a new entry per run) -- key by CONTENT like the eval cache (`%p-eval-cache-stem`), or skip them.
 c. THE INCLUDE PATH belongs in the key: the manifest hashes the file each `use` RESOLVED to, so a different `-I` that resolves the same name to a DIFFERENT file is not caught by the hash alone (`missing` covers only absent->present, #1284).  PROBE THIS FIRST (two `-I` dirs with different `B.pm` prototypes); the same hole may exist for modules under a changed /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3 and would then be its own task.
 d. SCRIPT-ONLY FACTS baked in at transpile time -- `$0`, `__FILE__`, `#line`, `caller`'s file, the `__END__`/DATA section: functions of path + content, so the key covers them; one guard row each (probe vs perl on a hit, not only on a miss).
 e. WHERE: the runtime owns the hit/miss logic exactly as `use` does (a `p-run-script-cached` beside `p-load-module-cached`), `pcl` only changes what it hands SBCL; entries under <cache>/modules/ (or a `scripts/` sibling -- decide, same prune either way).
 f. runpcl / the sweep / the companion do NOT use it (they measure the transpile).

BAR: `Pl/t/script-cache-01.t` (second run skips transpile AND compile, measured by the manifest/fasl mtimes; edit the script -> rebuild by mtime; edit ONLY a used module's prototype -> rebuild by the manifest; `-e` never caches; `--no-cache`; the `-I` case from (c); `$0`/`__FILE__`/DATA on a hit); `docs/caching.md` Â§2c; a DECIDED line; the gate; no emission change expected (no gen bump).  One agent session.

Related: #1188 (module fasl cache), #1261 (manifest), #1200 (eval cache), #1060 (`--executable` ran the program at build time), #756 (single binary -- a cached script fasl is its input), #1202 (extension load uncached).

ORDER (USER-confirmed s488): #1843 (the perl binary + PPI files in the compiler fingerprint) lands FIRST or in the same batch -- a cached main script would otherwise be the first entry that runs on a stale tokenizer without the path move that saves modules.
=== DONE (s488b) ===

SHIPPED: `pcl FILE` runs the program from a cache entry.  `pcl` hands SBCL
`(pcl::p-run-script-cached "<path as given>" "<pl2cl>" (list <-I dirs>)
(list <seed @INC>))` instead of transpiling to a temp .lisp, and the RUNTIME
owns hit/miss exactly as it does for a `use`.

STEP 1, THE INCLUDE-PATH PROBE (what the task asked for first) -- IT CHANGED
THE DESIGN.  Two `-I` dirs whose `B2.pm` differ only in an EMPTY PROTOTYPE
(`zap + 1` is `zap()+1` = 8 with it, `zap(+1)` = 107 without), three passes
d1 / d2 / d1 against one cache:

    subject                          -I d1   -I d2   -I d1
    perl                                 8     107       8
    pcl, MODULE reads the prototype      8       8       8   <- DIVERGES
    pcl, SCRIPT reads the prototype      8     107       8

  * The MODULE side has the hole and it is PRE-EXISTING (the manifest
    re-hashes the OLD path, which still exists and still hashes as read).
    First measurement of it; FILED as #1860, not fixed here.
  * The SCRIPT side is right today ONLY because the script is re-transpiled
    every run.  So caching it WITHOUT the include path in the key would have
    GIVEN scripts that bug.  Hence the key below.

THE ENTRY (`<cache>/scripts/`, its own directory so `--cache-info` can count
the population; everything else shared with modules/): `<stem>.lisp` +
`<stem>.deps` + `<stem>-<runtime-identity>.fasl`, stem = `%p-cache-stem` (the
module rule, extracted) over the absolute path, THE PATH AS GIVEN (`$0` is
that string verbatim), the cwd, the `-I` list in order, `PERL5LIB`, the
generation, "v2" and the compiler fingerprint.  Over-keying costs a MISS,
under-keying is a silent wrong; where they were in tension the key chose the
miss and says so.  Perl's own library dirs are NOT in the key: they are a
function of the perl binary, which #1843's fingerprint hashes.

SHARED MECHANISM (rule 11): `%p-cache-stem` (new, two callers),
`p-cache-valid-p` (gains an optional explicit manifest path, so it stays THE
ONE validity predicate -- three callers now: module, string eval, script),
`%p-note-entry-use` (extracted from `%p-note-cache-use`), `%p-prune-dir`,
`%p-build-module-fasl` / `%p-load-module-fasl`, `*pcl-fasl-build*` (so
compile-file does not run the body -- the #1060 rule, inherited).

PROGRAM MODE, NOT `--module`: `p-transpile-file` gained a MODE argument.  A
program gets its preamble AND the #339 drop announcement stays on, because a
dropped statement in the program the user is RUNNING is a diagnostic they must
see -- which is exactly why `--module` silences it.

THE COMPILE-POLICY EXEMPTION (`%p-compile-module-p`'s `:main-script` clause)
is the design question the task had to answer.  The directory lists exist
because a module under `-I`/PERL5LIB/`.` is probably being EDITED and a fasl
is the most opaque artifact PCL writes; a main script is ALWAYS under one of
those, so applying the module rule would pay the SBCL compile again on every
run -- 3.3 s of the 5.6 s, i.e. the whole prize.  The two OFF switches still
reach it (`PCL_NO_FASL_CACHE=1`, a `PCL_NO_COMPILE_DIRS` match, tested
BEFORE the clause), and `--no-cache` / `PCL_NO_CACHE` skip the whole thing.

THE SEED SEARCH PATH, discovered by measurement, not designed.  Two things
happen before the entry's own preamble runs, both resolving modules with @INC
still empty: (1) the compiler fingerprint locates PPI (#1843) -- with nothing
to search it recorded `ppi=0`, and that stamp then keyed every MODULE the
program loaded, splitting the module cache into a script-run population and
an everything-else one; (2) on a MISS, the program's own `use` statements,
which run at COMPILE-FILE time because that is what creates a module's
package before the reader meets a symbol in it.  So `pcl` passes the search
path its preamble is ABOUT to set, in the same order, in force only until the
preamble replaces it.  THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, also measured: with perl's
own library directories ahead of PCL's `lib/`, the compile-time `use Carp`
bound perl's REAL Carp.pm instead of PCL's shim and cached a transpile of it.

NOT CACHED, and `pcl` keeps the transpile-and-load path for them: `-e`/`-E`
and a file run with `-M` prefixes (a fresh random temp path per run, so a
path key leaks one dead entry per invocation -- content-keying them is
#1862), `--no-cache`/`PCL_NO_CACHE` (which also CHANGES the emission), and
`-c` (it must transpile and NOT run, the one thing this path cannot do).

MEASURED (best-of-5, warm core, cold entry, `uptime` load < 1):

    subject                        base run   cache MISS   cache HIT   perl
    hello.pl (1 line)                 0.181        0.203       0.033  0.006
    cl/pack-impl.pl (1,211 lines)     6.571        7.256       0.037  0.006

So the miss costs one run's worth (0.02 s / 0.69 s) and the hit is 5.5x /
178x.  `docs/caching.md` Â§5's table carries both rows.

GUARD `Pl/t/script-cache-01.t`, 51 rows, ~10 s: a second run skips BOTH the
transpile and the compile (asserted by the entry's mtimes, never by timing);
editing the script rebuilds by mtime; editing ONLY a used module's prototype
rebuilds through the manifest; `-e` leaves no path-keyed entry; `--no-cache`
bypasses; the step-1 `-I` case; `$0`, `__FILE__`, `caller`'s file and the
`__END__`/DATA section answer the same on a HIT as on a MISS and as perl
5.40.3; a script whose compile-file fails still runs (loud source fallback);
and a row over the four runners' text asserts that `runpcl`, the perl-tests
sweep, the companion suite and `pclperl-for-tests` never ask for a script
entry (they measure the transpile, and none goes through `pcl`).
Inverse-verified on a `git archive 11ef34a1` extraction: 7 failures and an
abort at row 45.

DEFAULT-ON vs OPT-IN IS THE USER'S OPEN DECISION, and it is ONE LINE in
`pcl`: `my $use_script_cache = defined($source) && !defined($inline) &&
!@use_mods && !$check_only && !$cache_off;` gains `$ENV{PCL_SCRIPT_CACHE} &&`
at the front.  Nothing else moves, because the runtime entry point is reached
only there.  The tree ships DEFAULT-ON (the argument: the prize is 5.5x on a
one-liner and 178x on a real program; the cost of a miss is one run's worth;
the `$0`/`__FILE__`/`caller`/DATA parity probes agree with perl on a hit; the
residual risk is that the key is wrong in a way the guards do not cover, and
the one hole MEASURED in the neighbourhood -- #1860 -- is the MODULE key's,
which a script entry does not inherit because its own key carries the
include path).

BY-PRODUCT, #1335 CLOSED: `pcl --cache-info` lists `evals/` and `scripts/`,
and `--clear-cache`'s glob names them -- it had never named the eval
directory while the help claimed it removed everything PCL made.

DOCS: `docs/caching.md` Â§2c (the script cache end to end) + the knobs table +
Â§5's measured rows; `docs/ir-spec.md` Â§9.2b ("the main script is an entry
too", normative, with the three rules that are the script's own); `pcl
--help` and `pcl`'s header; `docs/pcl-rollout-plan.md` Phase 6 and Phase 7
marked SUPERSEDED with a pointer (their `md5(path + mtime)` key and stat'ed
sidecar predate the content-hash manifest #1261 -- do not build them as
written); DECIDED + session-log.

NO EMISSION CHANGE: `tools/corpus-diff.pl` IDENTICAL over 111, silent drops 5
unchanged, no generation bump (the tree carries main's v2-1480).

Related: #1843 + #1861 (the fingerprint, same batch, landed first), #1860
(the module-key include-path hole this probe found), #1862 (`-e` and `-M`
content keying), #1335 (closed), #1188/#1261/#1200 (the mechanisms reused),
#756 (a single binary's input).


=== USER DECISION (s489, 2026-09-17 ~23:55) ===
DEFAULT-ON stays: "Keep it on by default."  (The USER first asked whether the script cache meant CPAN modules -- no: modules were already cached; this is the MAIN PROGRAM file `pcl FILE` runs.)  The one-line opt-in flip in `pcl` ~line 113 is documented but NOT taken.  #1860 (the shadowing-file resolution hole, both populations) is the first filler of the next session.
subject: DONE s488b: THE SCRIPT CACHE -- `pcl FILE` runs the program from a cache entry (p-run-script-cached, <cache>/scripts/, PROGRAM-mode pl2cl --deps, the :main-script compile-policy exemption); cl/pack-impl.pl 6.571 s -> 0.037 s, hello.pl 0.181 -> 0.033; the key carries the INCLUDE PATH because a -I move changes the parse (probed; the module key's same hole is #1860); -e / -M / -c not cached (#1862); DEFAULT-ON vs OPT-IN is one line and the USER's call
